page.title: Tutorial · tinyactors CLI
page.description: Compile an order chart, fix a misspelt timeout with tinyactors lint, trace the path to shipped and run an order session.

hero.headline: Compile, lint, draw and run an order chart
hero.lede: In seven commands, you compile an order chart and catch a misspelt timeout event with lint without running it. After the fix, a scripted session retries an unanswered charge after 30 seconds and ends in paid.

section.heading: 1. Compile the order chart
section.passage: Your order chart starts in open to collect items, moves to paying at checkout and sends a charge request for the order total. When the payment service does not answer within 30 seconds, paying sends a delayed timeout event so the order retries up to three times before moving to cancelled.

Save this chart as order.scxml and run tinyactors compile with -o so the compiler writes an image file at order.tai for your application. You will see zero diagnostics because the SCXML syntax is valid, which still leaves logic errors in your state transitions unchecked.

section.heading: 2. Catch unhandled events with lint
section.passage: Valid syntax does not guarantee your order can finish, so run tinyactors lint to inspect the chart's transition logic without executing a session. The linter compares events sent to the chart against its transitions, which lets you catch unhandled events before testing a live session.

The report shows one unhandled-event warning in paying because that state sends payment.timeout to the chart while its transitions listen for payment.timedout. Without a matching transition, an order whose payment service never answers misses the 30-second timeout event and stays in paying instead of retrying or cancelling.

section.heading: 3. Fix the event and check again
section.passage: Update both transitions in paying from payment.timedout to payment.timeout so their event list matches what the state sends after 30 seconds. Changing both lines fixes the retry loop when attempts < 3 and restores the final transition to cancelled after three failed attempts.

Next, run tinyactors check with -W to validate order.scxml and turn compiler warnings into errors without writing an output file. Seeing Valid: yes and zero diagnostics confirms that the updated chart compiles with neither syntax errors nor warnings.

Now run tinyactors lint with --deny all so any remaining warning or note fails the command with exit code 1. Because both transitions now handle payment.timeout, lint reports zero findings and exits with 0, which shows no unhandled timeout events remain.

section.heading: 4. Trace the path to shipped
section.passage: Run tinyactors path with --to shipped to verify that an order starting in open can reach the final shipped state. The output lists three transitions through paying and paid and notes the total > 0 condition on checkout, so an order must have a positive total before charging.

section.heading: 5. Draw the order chart
section.passage: Run tinyactors graph with -f svg and redirect the output to order.svg to inspect your order chart as state boxes and labelled transition routes. The resulting diagram adapts to your system's light or dark setting and lets you verify that paying loops back to itself on retries before reaching paid or cancelled.

drawing.alt: The order chart showing open, paying, paid, shipped and cancelled, with paying's retry looping back to itself

section.heading: 6. Run an order session
section.passage: To test your retry flow, save these JSON-RPC requests in session.jsonl so you can pipe them into tinyactors run one request per line. The script spawns an order actor, adds a pen priced at 1200, sends checkout, advances the clock by 30 seconds and answers the second charge.

Run tinyactors run with --io-processor payments and redirect session.jsonl to standard input so your session handles outgoing payments requests without an external service. When the order enters paying, the command writes an effect.send notification for each charge event, which lets your script observe and answer outgoing payment requests.

Request 4 leaves the actor idle with a 30-second deadline, so advancing the clock in request 5 lets request 6 fire payment.timeout and emit a second charge notification. Request 7 then supplies charge.ok, which cancels the next 30-second deadline in request 8 when the actor leaves paying. Request 9 inspects the actor state and finds it in paid.

section.heading: Put the checks in your build
section.passage: Once your chart works locally, run check and lint in CI so your build catches syntax errors or unhandled events before a pull request merges. You can pair those checks with fmt and diff, or drive sessions from a script that pauses and answers outgoing sends.

item.text: Automate check, lint, fmt and diff on every pull request.

term.link: Drive a host from a script

item.text: Pause an outgoing send until your script replies to it.
